title: Why he moved from trombone to bass; Piron's trio
summary: He repeats that the three-trombone band had no bass, and mentions playing string bass with Piron's trio at a country club and the Royal Palm Garden.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: I don't know what y'all, what the job.
We covered all those pictures for one thing, the picture with your band and all of that. I was just wondering if there's anything in particular that you had in mind.
I'd like to ask you a question. I saw him in that picture with the trombone. What band would leave the trombone and go on the bass? I explained that.
I think you explained that all right. Yeah. Yeah. See, by being in that brass band, they had three trombones. And they said they couldn't use three trombones. They didn't have no bass player.
So it made me start with bass.
With the string bass though. With any band? I played with the... What do you see in the line? ...Piron's...

...trio out at the country club too. Oh yeah. When Tom and me had a big band, he had a... He had a regular spot. They had the Royal Palm Garden. I think that was Delachez and Saratoa, where they had a dance. Yeah.
